questions.key_step: Recognise the linear form with integrating factor e^{-1/x}.
questions.justification: Standard linear equation; the only work is the t=-1/x integral and applying the condition. Routine chain of three standard steps, no insight, like 2026-P2-Q3.

questions.key_step: Put y^2=t (or y=vx); one substitution makes it linear/separable.
questions.justification: Two valid routes, each a standard substitution followed by a short integration; clean chain, no insight. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q3 (separable DE).

questions.key_step: Recognise Bernoulli (y^3 term) and use t=1/y^2.
questions.justification: Bernoulli with n=3 followed by integration by parts with logarithm, then constant. Chain of 4 stages, the Bernoulli form is the only idea; all routine. Slightly above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) because of the by-parts and the option algebra.

questions.key_step: Observe every term of the solution decays (alpha, beta > 0).
questions.justification: One integrating-factor solve and a limit of decaying exponentials; a single familiar move. Placed at 1 as the answer needs no computation beyond the standard formula.

questions.key_step: Separate variables and read the limit off the exponent.
questions.justification: Immediate separation and a one-line limit; single familiar move. Like 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).

questions.key_step: Integrating factor ln x, then integrate x ln x by parts.
questions.justification: Linear DE with a slightly non-obvious integrating factor and an integration by parts; routine chain of 4 steps. Same as 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: t = tan^{-1}x^3 turns the integrating factor integral into ∫ t sin t dt and the exponentials cancel.
questions.justification: Heavy-looking linear equation where the unusual substitution t=tan^{-1}x^3 is the idea and the cancellation of exponentials must be spotted; idea availability is lower than for a routine linear equation. One level above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).

questions.key_step: y = vx and splitting (v^2+3)/(v+1)^3 by writing the numerator in powers of (v+1).
questions.justification: Homogeneous substitution gives a repeated-factor partial fraction and a back-substitution simplification where one slip changes the option; chain of 4-5 standard stages. Careful but standard, so rated 3 rather than 2.

questions.key_step: Differentiate to a linear DE; recover f(3)=2 from the original equation.
questions.justification: Integral equation converted to a linear DE, one substitution and the condition from x=3; three routine stages, no insight beyond standard technique.

questions.key_step: y = tx gives ∫(1-t²)/(3t-t³) as a logarithm; ask only for 3x²y-y³.
questions.justification: Homogeneous substitution with a logarithmic integral and an implicit relation evaluated at x=2 without solving for y; same demand as Q8 in this paper, less partial fractions. Chain of 4-5 standard stages.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor sec x, then by parts on x sec² x.
questions.justification: Single linear equation with a by-parts integral and an option-matching simplification; three standard steps, no insight.

questions.key_step: y² = t makes it linear (or s = xy² makes it separable).
questions.justification: One substitution, a linear equation with a simple integrating factor and matching the form; short routine chain, no insight.

questions.key_step: Treat ∫₀²f as a constant k; determine k from k = ∫₀²f.
questions.justification: Constant-integral trick, a linear equation and a self-consistency equation for k; four routine stages in numerical format, no options.

questions.key_step: Recognise (1+ln x)dx = d(x ln x) and put t = x ln x.
questions.justification: One well-chosen substitution making the equation linear in t, then a resonant integral and a condition; asked quantity needs only α ln α. Chain of 3 routine steps.

questions.key_step: Homogeneous (y=vx) or t=y² - both reduce it to a one-line integral.
questions.justification: Standard homogeneous equation; three short stages; the chain is routine.

questions.key_step: y dx + x dy = d(xy); separate in u = xy and fix the modulus sign by the region u > 1.
questions.justification: Exact-differential recognition, partial fractions, modulus/sign handling and a final algebraic solve with four close options; a careful chain where the sign case can silently flip the option. Slightly above 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: Partial fractions for the integrating factor x⁵/(1+x⁵); the right side then collapses to x³ + x⁻².
questions.justification: Linear equation whose integrating factor needs a partial-fraction/substitution step; then cancellation and exact arithmetic with close options. Four routine stages.

questions.key_step: Bernoulli with y² on the right: t = 1/y; integrating factor √(1+x²).
questions.justification: Bernoulli recognition then a standard integrating factor and ∫dx/√(1+x²); routine chain.

questions.key_step: Two solutions of the same first-order ODE never meet; their difference is Ce^x ≠ 0.
questions.justification: Immediate once the solution is written; single familiar fact (solutions of a first-order ODE do not cross).

questions.key_step: t = ln(y+2) makes the equation linear in x with integrating factor √t.
questions.justification: Dependent-variable switch, a substitution and a linear equation with half-integer powers, then two evaluations; routine multi-step chain.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor x sec x; the asked expression is (xy)'' = -xy.
questions.justification: Linear DE with an unfamiliar integrating factor, then recognition that xy''+2y' is (xy)'' and a closed-form evaluation; numerical answer with no option check.

questions.key_step: y-intercept of the tangent is f - xf'; this equals d(f/x)·(-x²).
questions.justification: Geometry of the tangent gives a first-order equation that is an exact derivative of f/x; then two point conditions and a distance; numerical format, three conceptual stages.

questions.key_step: Rewrite as linear in y; integrating factor √(ln x).
questions.justification: Linear equation with an unusual but routine integrating factor and a logarithmic power integral; short chain.

questions.key_step: L = ln cos y, dL = -tan y dy; the linear equation in x has integrating factor L³ and the constant turns out zero.
questions.justification: Needs the right change of variable, three-stage linear solve with logarithms of cosines and exact matching of the final form (m,n); numerical, no options, precision risk in signs.

questions.key_step: Section formula plus intercepts give x y' = -k y; then k = 2 from the two points.
questions.justification: Geometry to differential equation, solving for k, then a log integral; key says Bonus because the asked expression is not an integer. Four stages with exact algebra, numerical format.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor (x²-1)²; match 2ln(√2+1)+1-√3 to the given form.
questions.justification: Linear equation with a pair of standard integrals and a final pattern match to natural numbers; chain of 4 routine steps in numerical format.

questions.key_step: The condition fixes e^{a-b}=4/3; then x=y means (4/3)^t = 2.
questions.justification: Two exponentials, one condition and a logarithm base conversion to match the form; simple chain, no insight.

questions.key_step: Partial fractions on both sides; 'slope never zero' fixes the sign inside the modulus.
questions.justification: Separable equation with two partial-fraction integrals, a modulus-sign decision and algebra to an option; routine but several places to slip.

questions.key_step: d(1+cos²x) = -sin 2x dx, so the integrating factor is 1 + cos²x.
questions.justification: Linear equation with a logarithmic-derivative coefficient; integrating factor is immediate and the rest is a one-line integral. Two-three routine steps.

questions.key_step: xy' - y = x² d(y/x): put y/x = t, and cos t dt = dx/x.
questions.justification: One recognisable substitution and a one-line integral, then plugging the condition; single familiar move.

questions.key_step: The integrand is the exact derivative of (x²-2x) sin x, so y(2)=y(0).
questions.justification: Two integrations by parts (or the exact-derivative recognition) and evaluation at x=2 where everything vanishes; a few routine steps.

questions.key_step: sec x - sin x tan x = cos x; then the equation is linear with homogeneous solution tan x.
questions.justification: Trigonometric simplification then a linear equation whose integrating factor needs ∫csc; moderate chain, routine.

questions.key_step: x = vy and ∫dv/(v ln v) = ln ln v.
questions.justification: Homogeneous equation in the x-as-function form with a ln ln integral and a modulus match with the options; short chain, routine.

questions.key_step: Excess over the surrounding temperature halves every 15 time units.
questions.justification: Standard Newton-cooling separable equation; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: t = x+y gives a separable equation; then z = t² (or u = t⁻²) is needed to integrate.
questions.justification: Substitution, a second substitution/partial fractions with a quartic denominator, constant and an exponential solve into an option; longer chain than a plain linear equation with a bit more precision risk.

questions.key_step: Check consistency: f→1 at -∞ needs α>0 and equilibrium -3/α=1, i.e. α=-3 - contradiction.
questions.justification: Solving is trivial; the level comes from noticing the conditions contradict each other (no options help). Idea availability is moderate: students who stop at α=-3 mark 9.

questions.key_step: t = 2x+3y; the integral splits as 2 + 9/(t-8); divide the result by 3 to match the given form.
questions.justification: Parallel-lines substitution, polynomial division in the integrand and a final matching of a prescribed form with three unknowns, in numerical format with no option check.

questions.key_step: Shift the origin to (1,1) to get a homogeneous equation; (1-t)/(1+t²) integrates to tan⁻¹t - ½ln(1+t²).
questions.justification: Non-parallel-lines shift, homogeneous substitution and a standard arctan/log integral, then matching constants; routine chain in numerical format.

questions.key_step: Separate variables; recognise the final angle as π/4 - 3/2 and use the tangent subtraction formula.
questions.justification: Single separable equation with one substitution integral and a tangent identity to match the form; short chain.

questions.key_step: Evaluate the limit as x f f' - x³ e^{f/x} to get a homogeneous DE; then v e^{-v} dv = dx.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas: reading a limit as a derivative expression, then a homogeneous equation with ∫ve^{-v}; numerical and no options. Idea less familiar than a plain DE.

questions.key_step: Intercepts of the tangent, then the y² terms cancel and y'≠0 is divided out.
questions.justification: Geometry to differential equation with an algebraic expansion where the y² terms cancel, then a linear equation; numerical, precision in the setup. Four stages.

questions.key_step: t = tan x then u = 1/t gives a linear equation; at the initial point the combination e^{2y}tan x equals 1.
questions.justification: Two substitutions (Bernoulli) and an exponential evaluation; numerical answer with no options, the Bernoulli form is hidden in the variable choice.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor (t+1)⁻²: x/(t+1)² has derivative (t+1).
questions.justification: Single linear equation with power integrating factor; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: Treat x as the dependent variable: integrating factor 1/y.
questions.justification: Linear equation in x(y) with an immediate integrating factor; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: Factor the quartic as (x²+1)(x²+2x+2); the numerator is the sum of the two factors.
questions.justification: Factorisation, a partial-fraction split that is immediate once the sum is noticed, and two arctan integrals; routine.

questions.key_step: Factor 2x³y+8xy = 2xy(x²+4): integrating factor x²+4.
questions.justification: Linear equation, integrating factor by logarithmic derivative, one standard arctan integral; routine few steps.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor e^{2x}; the particular solution vanishes at π/8, leaving only the transient.
questions.justification: Linear equation with an exponential-times-trig integral and a clean evaluation; routine standard chain.

questions.key_step: Circle: x²+y²+g(x+y)=0 with one parameter; differentiate the constant ratio (x²+y²)/(x+y).
questions.justification: Formation of a first-order equation by eliminating one constant and simplifying to match an option; short routine algebra, familiar.

questions.key_step: Divide by 2x: the left side is d(y ln x)/dx.
questions.justification: Linear equation whose integrating factor is a logarithm and a by-parts integral; one subtlety (the singular point x=1) that the key ignores. Routine chain.

questions.key_step: t = tan⁻¹x turns (1+x²)d/dx into d/dt: constant-coefficient linear equation.
questions.justification: Substitution to a constant-coefficient linear equation, then two evaluation points; routine, familiar.

questions.key_step: β(x dy + y dx) = β d(xy): no xy term for a circle gives β=0; then equal x², y² coefficients give α=2.
questions.justification: Parametric differential equation, an exact-differential integration and a circle's conditions to decide parameters; unfamiliar-looking but each step is standard. More steps and two parameters to determine.

questions.key_step: t = e^{tan x}: the x-side is -dt/(1+t²); the final angle sum π/2 means y·e = 1.
questions.justification: Separable with a composite substitution and an arctan sum; routine.

questions.key_step: f = derivative of the area function; eliminate c₁, c₂: y''/y' = f''/f'.
questions.justification: Fundamental theorem to recover f, then elimination of two constants (second order); short routine chain.

questions.key_step: Multiply by sec y: z = tan y gives the linear equation z'+2xz = x³.
questions.justification: Reduction by sec y and z=tan y, a linear solve with a by-parts integral, then evaluation; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Integrate term by term; complete the square to read the vertex.
questions.justification: Immediate integration, completing the square; single familiar move.

questions.key_step: y=vx gives 5v dv/(1-4v²) = dx/x: a logarithm in 1-4v².
questions.justification: Homogeneous substitution with a logarithmic integral and log-algebra to match the option form; routine.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation: y'² + y² = 1, so y = sin x and y'' = -y.
questions.justification: Differentiation of an integral equation, a non-linear first-order equation with a branch choice (y≥0), and the observation y''=-y; the branch and the singular solution make it more delicate than a plain separable question.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor e^{-x}; by-parts integral of e^{-x} sin x; c = 0.
questions.justification: Standard linear equation with one by-parts integral; one familiar move chain.

questions.key_step: t = x+y+2 gives t' = 1+t²: y = tan x - x - 2, monotone increasing.
questions.justification: Substitution to a standard separable equation, endpoint extrema and surd arithmetic; three routine stages, numerical.

questions.key_step: The limit is a difference quotient; it gives 2xf - x²f' = 1, a linear equation.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas: reading the limit as a derivative combination and then solving a linear equation; numerical, no options.

questions.key_step: The integrating factor e^{-1/(1+x²)} is exactly the factor in f: f(x) = x²/2.
questions.justification: Linear equation with a cancelling integrating factor, then a standard parabola-line area; routine.

questions.key_step: Slope condition gives (y+5)² = 9(x-3); focal distance = x - 3 + a.
questions.justification: Differential equation from a slope condition leading to a conic, recognise the parabola, then focal distance; two chapters but each step is standard.

questions.key_step: The equation is exact: d[(e^y+1) sin x] = 0.
questions.justification: Immediate separation/exactness and one evaluation; single familiar move.

questions.key_step: Divide by xy: d ln|y/x| + d(xy) = 0.
questions.justification: Division by xy splits into exact differentials; one integral and a matching step; routine short chain.

questions.key_step: The limit at -∞ equals the equilibrium -α/3, so α = -21.
questions.justification: Linear (separable) equation and a limit condition fixing the constant; short chain, familiar.
